input.brief: AUDIT/WEB: Awwwards-caliber deterministic website quality, accessibility, typography, and UX inspection instrument

direction.name: Dressed as something else
direction.idea: Art-direct the subject as if it belonged to a different, more vivid category. A money app is sold like a streetwear drop. An industrial roaster is presented like a design object. Drilling hardware gets the calm of a watch brand. A parcel-locker service becomes a fairground of stickers. Choose the borrowed category by asking what feeling the audience is missing from this kind of product (swagger, calm, glamour, play) and which category owns that feeling. Then take its manners completely: its type, its pacing, its way of photographing things. The contrast between dull subject and vivid dress is what people remember.
direction.composition: Depends on the borrowed category, so decide it explicitly and write it in your notes. Fashion drop: one shouted condensed headline across the full width, a single cropped image under it, then product facts as a blunt list. Watch or perfume: a centred object on a dark field, a small serif name, very few words, long vertical pauses. Poster or zine: flat colour blocks, heavy type, tilted cut-out images. Museum: one item per screen on a plinth-like band of colour with a short label beside it. Whichever you choose, the page structure stays simple (four to six sections) and every section uses the borrowed manners, including pricing and the footer.
direction.typography: The borrowed category's type, fully committed: condensed and loud, or refined and small. No halfway.
direction.colour: The borrowed category's palette, which will be unlike the subject's sector norm. That mismatch is intended.
direction.imagery: Photograph the subject the way the borrowed category would be photographed. With the dealt set, choose images for attitude, not literal relevance, and crop them hard.
direction.richness: Attitude. The page has a recognisable voice from another world, applied to a subject nobody expected it for.
direction.pitfalls: Name the borrowed category in one word before you start, or the result is merely loud. The content must still be clear: what it is, what it costs, how to get it. Avoid borrowing from 'tech startup', which is the default you are escaping.

hero.name: Shouted headline, rising photograph
hero.blueprint: Borrowed from a fashion drop. A near-white or single flat colour field. Navigation is one compact line at the top on 24px margins: condensed wordmark left, three text links centred, the single action right. Directly beneath, a two-line uppercase headline in a bold condensed face at clamp(88px, 11.4vw, 176px), centred, leading 0.88, tracking -0.02em, about 60% of the viewport wide; it occupies the band from 12% to 43% of the height. Immediately under the second line, pulled up with a negative margin of -1.2vw so its top edge tucks behind the letters' baseline, a single portrait photograph rises: 27% of the viewport wide (columns 5-8), 3:4, square corners, object-fit: cover, cropped by the bottom edge so only its upper two thirds show. The photograph is the only colour on the screen. The flanks either side of it stay empty apart from one supporting sentence at 17px bottom-left in a 280px column, and the price or key fact at the same size bottom-right, both on a baseline 32px above the bottom edge.
hero.mobile: The headline sets at 17vw on two lines, flush to 16px margins and filling the width, in the top third of the screen. The photograph widens to 64% of the width, centred, 3:4, starting directly under the headline and running off the bottom. The supporting sentence and the key fact move below the fold. Navigation collapses to the wordmark and the action.
hero.headline: A blunt 2-4 word statement in condensed capitals, at most 22 characters, one or two words per line.

photos.title: Architecture
photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors

photos.alt: White arched bridge spanning grey water under a pale sky
Tall pointed vaults and pale columns of a church interior
Small figure walking past a huge bright yellow wall
White angular concrete building against a black sky

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Output index, live sheet
sections.blueprint: For products that make documents: invoices, reports, emails, statements. Columns 1–5 list the names of three to five outputs, one per line, at clamp(36px, 4vw, 64px), leading 1.1, each a `<button>`; the selected name is in full ink, the rest in the soft ink. There is no other heading. Columns 7–12 are a stage in a flat tone one step from the ground, 88svh tall, and on it lies the selected output as an object: a paper-white sheet 560px wide, built in HTML at true size, root marked data-ui, with a real sender, real line items, sums that add up and a date. The sheet starts 72px below the stage's top and runs past its bottom edge, which crops it. Selecting a name swaps the sheet with a 200ms crossfade; an email is narrower (440px), a receipt narrower still (300px), all left-aligned 64px into the stage.
sections.mobile: Names become one sideways-scrolling row at 22px with scroll-snap, the selected one in full ink. Beneath, the stage fills the width and is 70svh tall; the sheet keeps its true size, anchored top-left with a 16px inset and cropped by the stage's right and bottom edges. Tapping a name swaps it.

sections.name: Paragraph with picture words
sections.blueprint: One paragraph does the work of a feature grid. Three or four sentences, 35–50 words in total, set at clamp(30px, 3.6vw, 60px), leading 1.18, medium weight, across columns 1–11, left-aligned. Each sentence names one capability, and directly after that capability's key noun sits an inline slot: an inline-block frame 1em tall and 1.9em wide, radius 0.18em, dropped 0.12em below the baseline, holding a tight photograph crop (object-fit: cover) or a real interface control at readable size. Four slots at most, never two on one line. The nouns keep the weight and colour of the rest; the slots are the only emphasis. Mark it up as a paragraph and give the section a visually hidden heading of two or three words; nothing visible sits above. 72px lower, starting at column 7, one supporting sentence at 18px and the action.
sections.mobile: The paragraph drops to 7vw with leading 1.22 and fills the width. Slots stay inline at 1em tall but narrow to 1.5em wide. If a slot lands alone at the start of a line, let it; do not shrink the type. The supporting sentence and the action follow at full width.

sections.name: Accordion of tinted panels
sections.blueprint: A two-column introduction, then one horizontal accordion. Introduction: the heading, two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), in columns 1–5; one paragraph at 18px in columns 7–11. 64px below, a flex row across columns 1–12, 520px tall, of four to six panels with no gaps. The open stage is a panel taking about 58% of the width; the rest are vertical slivers sharing what remains. Order is carried by colour: the first stage is the darkest tone of one hue and each later stage is a lighter flat tint of it, so the row reads dark to light from left to right. A sliver shows only its stage name, rotated 90 degrees and reading upward, at 20px bold, anchored to its bottom-left. The open panel shows the name at 40px top-left, a 36ch paragraph at 18px bottom-left and, optionally, one photograph in its right half. Clicking a sliver opens it (flex-basis transition, 450ms).
sections.mobile: The accordion turns vertical: stages stack at full width as bars 64px tall in the same dark-to-light order, names set horizontally at 18px. The open stage expands to its content height with the paragraph at 17px. The first stage is open by default.

sections.name: Names running off the edges
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed band in a flat colour, about 34vh tall, holding a single line of names that is cropped by both viewport edges. The names are set at 8vw in the display weight, `white-space: nowrap`, separated by a solid round dot one third of the cap height, and the line moves slowly to the left (a CSS `translateX` animation over 40 seconds on a duplicated track, paused under `prefers-reduced-motion`). The band has no heading. Its meaning comes from one sentence at 18px set directly below the band at the left margin on the page ground, stating plainly who these names are. Supplied logos may replace names if all are available as single-colour SVGs at 0.8em height; do not mix logos and set names in one line. The band butts against the sections above and below with no gap.
sections.mobile: The band is 22vh tall with names at 15vw, still cropped at both edges and still moving. The explaining sentence sits under it at 16px with 20px margins. Do not add a second line running the opposite way; one line is the idea.

sections.name: One word is the button
sections.blueprint: The entire band is one link. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, about 60svh tall, contains a single verb of four to eight letters set at 24–30vw in the heaviest weight, tight tracking, sized with `clamp()` so it spans the content width on one line with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The `<a>` wraps the whole band; on hover and focus the field and the word swap colours instantly. In the top-left corner, at 20px, one sentence says what happens next; in the top-right, an arrow drawn as a simple inline SVG, 48px, points up and right. There is no other button anywhere in the section. In a page with a motif, the band's top corners take the motif's shape (a large radius, or a chamfer cut with `clip-path`). Keep the word honest: the action itself, not a slogan.
sections.mobile: The band is 46svh tall. The word is set at whatever size fills the width on one line; choose a shorter verb rather than going below 22vw. Sentence top-left at 17px across two lines, arrow top-right at 32px. The whole band stays tappable.

sections.name: Invitation over a cropped name
sections.blueprint: Close and footer in one full-viewport field of the inverse colour. Upper third, columns 1–7: a two-line invitation at about 5vw, three to five words, with one filled rectangular button beneath it. At columns 10–12, top-aligned with the invitation, three or four social or contact links stacked at 16px. The wordmark fills the bottom of the screen at 26–30vw on one line, `white-space: nowrap`, heavier and larger than the viewport can hold: it is pushed down with `transform: translateY(30%)` so the bottom edge cuts through the letters, and a long name also runs off the right edge. `overflow: hidden` on the footer does the cropping. One row of credits and legal links at 13px sits directly above the wordmark's cap line, spread left and right. The cropped name must be recognisable from its upper two-thirds alone; test that it is.
sections.mobile: Invitation at 11vw on two lines at the top with a full-width button. Links follow as one row of words at 15px. The wordmark sits at 34vw at the bottom, cropped by both the bottom and the right edge, with the legal row above it at 12px.

references.name: Moto Finance
references.idea: A metal card presented like a museum piece: lit by a single overhead light box in a black room, then orbiting through dim architectural stills.
references.hero: Black full-bleed 3D scene. A pale silver-lavender light panel, a trapezoid in perspective like a ceiling light box, occupies the top 20% and centre 55% of the viewport. The two-line uppercase headline, centred at 4.4vw in medium grotesk with tight leading, straddles the panel's lower edge so its first line sits half on light, half on black. In the exact centre a small metal card stands on a low plinth, only about 150px wide, surrounded by darkness. A light-grey pill button (about 250 by 52px) is centred near the bottom; the logo is top-left and a dark pill button top-right.
references.type: Neue Montreal only: weight 500 uppercase at 64px (4.4vw) with near-zero tracking and leading under 1.0 for headings, 20px sentence case for body, tiny caps labels in the footer. Three sizes; centred until the left-aligned footer.
references.colour: #080808 #edefef #c4cbd6 #e1e5e5 #2a2f3a — Black with cool silver-grey and no brand colour at all. One section inverts to pale grey-white with grey type; the only chroma is amber city lights and a blue atmosphere rim on the globe.
references.imagery: Rendered chrome card with an embossed profile medallion, a night-side Earth, and small dim architectural and fashion stills floating as tilted panels in 3D. Everything underexposed, cool and low-saturation.
references.layout: Full-viewport scenes stacked one per screen, each with a centred uppercase heading, an optional short sub-line and a pill button. One light interlude breaks the black. The footer switches to a left-aligned statement with link columns at the far right.

sections.description: Centred heading at the top with a two-line grey sub-line and a pale pill button directly under it. The lower 45% is the top arc of a night-side Earth rising from the bottom edge, about 75% of the viewport wide, with city lights and a bright blue-white rim on the upper right. Three small dark capsule labels with check icons float over and beside the globe at staggered positions, like status notifications.

A dark 3D room: about twelve small photo panels (roughly 70 by 90px, each tilted at its own angle, heavily dimmed) arranged in two loose rows across the full width, receding with blur. The card stands edge-on in the centre, much larger, catching a specular highlight. Later the card faces front at top-centre and a centred two-line heading with a pill button sits under it.

A pale grey-white band. Two tall columns of currency amounts in mid-size light-grey sans, one at a quarter and one at three-quarters of the width, each fading to white at top and bottom like slot-machine reels, with the centre rows darkest. Between them, three short centred lines of small black text. The bottom edge of the band reveals a dark photograph.

steal: Let a headline straddle the edge of a light shape so one line is half on light and half on dark.
Show the product very small in a large dark space in the first viewport, then let it grow as the page scrolls.
Use vertically scrolling columns of real-looking figures, faded at both ends, as a quiet backdrop for a three-line statement.

references.name: Locker Land
references.idea: A dry B2B parcel-locker pitch dressed as a fairground of die-cut stickers, where the main navigation is a fan of five tilted illustrated cards.
references.hero: Post-red field overlaid with a faint lighter-red square grid. Small white brand lock-up top-left; a white pill button with a hard dark-red offset shadow top-right. Top-centre, a two-line sticker-style logo (cream letters, thick cream outline, small locker drawing) about 20% of viewport width. Beneath it a two-line centred white sentence at 18px; no larger headline. The lower half is a fan of five portrait cards with thick coloured frames and rounded corners: centre card upright, neighbours rotated about 8 degrees, the outer pair about 18 degrees and cropped by the viewport edges, each with a label tab overlapping its bottom edge. A two-line caption sits centred below.
references.type: apDisplay, a brand grotesque, is the only family: weight 500, sentence case, slightly tight. Body 16-18px; section headings in dark red reach about 5.9vw. The hero has no typographic headline, the sticker logo plays that role. Labels inside sticker tabs go bold.
references.colour: #dc1928 #fdf3db #952625 #e0a912 #5b7a94 #d46831 — Post red and cream alternate as full section fields; mustard, slate blue, burnt orange and maroon are reserved for card frames and badges. Warm, flat, no gradients.
references.imagery: Flat vector drawings (parcel, locker, hand holding a card) with thick cream die-cut outlines and hard offset shadows, plus candid photos of people at lockers placed inside arch-shaped cut-outs and wide rounded video tiles.
references.layout: Every section is a centre-stacked composition on a full-width colour field, with a pill-shaped sticky sub-nav top-centre after the hero. Sections are separated by ornament rather than whitespace: a red and cream checkerboard strip, a scalloped awning edge. Cards come in tilted rows of three or five.

sections.description: On red beneath a checkerboard strip, a dark-red pill with a dotted inner border holds the heading. Three statistics are scattered as tilted stickers instead of a row: a mustard circle, a maroon starburst seal with a cursor-arrow sticker overlapping it, and a slate-blue tag shape, each with a small parcel or locker illustration tucked onto a corner. Figures are large; captions are tiny and centred inside each shape.

On cream, the heading sits in a white rounded box with dark-red outline and offset shadow, hanging directly under the sticky nav. Below, three equal portrait cards in mustard, slate blue and orange, each with a dark-red border and hard offset shadow, containing an arch-shaped photo cut-out of people, a tilted name-tag sticker, a starburst date badge, two centred lines of copy and a small white pill button.

A centred locker illustration with icon stickers orbiting it, a centred heading and two-line intro, then a full-width two-by-two mosaic of video stills with no gaps and rounded outer corners. Each tile carries one large white rounded chip with a bold red word, placed low and off-centre. A hand-drawn orange arrow sticker overlaps the mosaic's top-left corner, pointing in.

Five stacked white pill-shaped rows in a centred column about 65% of the page wide, each with dark-red outline, hard offset shadow, question at left and chevron at right. A checkerboard strip then returns the page to red, where an oversized version of the sticker logo sits centred with a one-line copyright beneath.

steal: Turn the primary navigation into a fan of tilted illustrated cards in the hero, centre card upright and the outer ones rotated and cropped by the viewport edges.
Give every element the same die-cut sticker treatment (thick cream outline plus a hard, unblurred offset shadow in a darker shade of the background) so buttons, cards and badges read as one family.
Present statistics as differently shaped badges (circle, starburst, tag) scattered at angles rather than as three equal columns.

references.name: The Content Architecture
references.idea: The product name becomes a rotating vortex of concentric text rings that you scroll into, and the sales argument is a ticking hours-lost counter beside an itemised receipt.
references.hero: Exact 50/50 vertical split. The left half is warm cream with a left-aligned stack starting a third of the way down at an 80px margin: one-line mono caps label, a two-line medium-weight sans headline at only 3vw, a four-line grey paragraph capped near 510px, then a black button notched into two joined halves beside a pale grey secondary. A mono scroll cue with a target glyph sits bottom-left. The right half is a charcoal canvas filled with concentric rings of white mono caps spiralling round a centre and cropped by the viewport. A dark boxed nav with a marquee strip floats top-centre across the seam; a minimap thumbnail sits top-right.
references.type: GeistMono carries two thirds of the page: caps labels, nav, buttons and receipt rows with dot leaders. GeistSans 500 sets quiet 43px sentence-case headlines with zero tracking. The only loud size is a counter numeral near 18vw, so three sizes in total.
references.colour: #f1eee7 #232323 #dedede #f28a1c #000000 — Warm cream and charcoal trade places section by section. A single small orange dot marks the paid action on the button and nav; no other hue appears.
references.imagery: No photographs. Canvas-drawn concentric rings of the product name in white mono over a faint dotted grid, later dissolving into scattered glyphs and inverted text fragments. Full-bleed and cropped by the viewport.
references.layout: An 80px left margin holds every text block. Headlines stay small at the top-left of tall cream sections while one oversized element (vortex, numeral, receipt) takes the opposite side. Floating nav, minimap and a help tab stay pinned throughout.

sections.description: Scroll transition between hero and first section: the camera pushes into the text vortex, rings scaling until letters are hundreds of pixels tall and cropped at every edge, the dotted grid showing between them. A solid cream disc opens at the centre and grows until it becomes the next section's background. A full-screen wipe built from the hero's own artwork, with the nav still floating above.

Pinned cream section. Top-left, a three-line 43px headline with a two-line grey note. Bottom-left, a tilde-prefixed numeral about 18vw tall counts from 00 to 24 as you scroll, with a mono caption and small chip beneath. On the right a receipt column framed by dashed rules fills line by line: mono caps rows grouped by day, dot leaders running to right-aligned hour values, the newest row inverted white on black.

The cream page ends in a band where the vortex returns as debris: tiny mono fragments, some inverted in black boxes, scattered sparsely and thickening upward into the dark ring pattern. Below it a plain footer: logo mark with a stacked two-line name on the left, two short mono caps link columns on the right, and a builder credit bottom-right.

steal: Split the primary button into two notched halves so a two-word action reads like a physical ticket, with one orange dot as the page's only accent.
Argue the cost of doing nothing with a pinned counter: a huge numeral ticks up while itemised mono rows with dot leaders append beside it.
Build the hero graphic from the brand name set on concentric rotating rings, then reuse it as the scroll transition and as footer debris.
